metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The lingering psychological presence or memory of a person who is physically absent.
acceptable_visual_variants: A faint, double-exposure style figure standing behind the speaker
A soft, dark silhouette cast on a wall that does not match the speaker's own posture
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: his physical shadow cast by light
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: An illustrator might draw a literal dark silhouette on the ground, which misses the emotional sense of a haunting memory.
metaphor_spans.tenor: the persistent memory or psychological presence of the stranger
metaphor_spans.vehicle: a physical shadow cast by a person
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a faint, translucent silhouette or a soft, glowing outline of a figure standing near the speaker in an otherwise empty room.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The emotional impact or lingering impression left by a past moment.
acceptable_visual_variants: A faint, glowing footprint on a dusty floor
A soft, faded impression of a hand on a surface
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: a physical mark, scar, or footprint
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Drawing a physical scar or a literal footprint on the floor would look like a crime scene or physical injury rather than a nostalgic memory.

metaphor_spans.tenor: the emotional impression of a past moment
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Represent this abstractly through a faded, glowing footprint or a faint handprint on a windowpane or mirror.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation collapses the distinct emotional nuances of 'yaad' (memory) and 'ahsaas' (feeling/perception) into generic English terms, losing the specific internal sensory texture of the Hindi words.
The translation of 'beeta pal' (past moment) as 'that moment' loses the explicit sense of time having passed or elapsed carried by the participle 'beeta'.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The overwhelming, heavy, and continuous emotional impact of the stranger's silence.
acceptable_visual_variants: A stylized, abstract scene where dark, rain-like streaks fall across a glowing heart silhouette
A person standing under a localized dark cloud of rain indoors, symbolizing isolation
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: his lack of speech physically rains down like water onto a physical heart organ
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: A literal depiction of water raining onto an anatomical heart would look grotesque or surreal in a medical sense.

metaphor_spans.source_term: उसकी खामोशी अब भी दिल पर बरसती है
metaphor_spans.tenor: the heavy emotional impact of silence on the speaker's feelings
metaphor_spans.vehicle: rain falling heavily on a surface
metaphor_spans.visualization_strategy: Depict a person sitting indoors looking out at a heavy downpour, with the rain reflecting on the windowpane casting tear-like shadows across their chest.

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The translation of 'aahat' as 'footsteps' narrows a highly evocative Hindi sensory term that refers to any soft, subtle sound of someone's approach (like the rustle of clothes or a soft breath) to just the sound of feet.
The translation of 'aks' (reflection/shadow/image) as 'image' loses the Urdu-derived poetic resonance of a mirrored reflection or ghostly double, flattening it to a visual sight.
The translation of 'poochunga main' (I will ask) loses the explicit masculine grammatical gender marking of the speaker ('poochunga' vs feminine 'poochungi') in the English translation.

annotation.theme: The lingering presence of a dreamlike stranger and the persistent mystery of their connection.

original_poem:
वह अजनबी जो कल रात सपनों में आया था,  
हैरान हूँ, उसकी परछाई मेरे साथ क्यों है।  
कोई याद, कोई अहसास, कोई छूटा हुआ  
बीता पल – उसी का निशान आज भी साथ क्यों है।

कितनी रातें गुज़र गईं, उसकी आहट नहीं आई,  
फिर भी दिल को क्यों लगता है कि वह पास है।  
वह अजनबी जो कल रात सपनों में आया था,  
उसकी खामोशी अब भी दिल पर बरसती है।

शायद किसी रोज़ इस राह से गुज़रे वह,  
शायद उसका अक्स मुझे फिर दिखाई दे।  
फिर से पूछूँगा मैं उससे यह सवाल,  
कि वह अजनबी अब भी अजनबी क्यों है।
translated_poem:
That stranger who visited my dreams last night,  
Why does his shadow still linger with me?  
Some memory, some feeling, something left behind –  
The mark of that moment, why does it stay with me still?

So many nights have passed without his footsteps,  
Yet my heart feels he is still close.  
That stranger who visited my dreams last night,  
His silence still rains upon my heart.

Perhaps someday he will pass this way,  
Perhaps I’ll see his image once again.  
And I’ll ask him the question once more,  
Why does that stranger remain a stranger?
